title: There are no maps between bounded above complexes over a regular ring when their support ranges are separated by the dimension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement says that over a Noetherian regular ring of finite dimension d there are no maps in the derived category between a bounded above complex vanishing in degrees at most k and a bounded above complex vanishing in degrees at least k minus d plus one (statement lines 20766-20772). The proof normalizes the first complex, reduces by a double induction on the top degree to the case of a single module placed in one degree, resolves that module by projectives of length at most d using finite global dimension, and then observes that the two representatives have disjoint supports so that no map of complexes between them exists (proof lines 20774-20796). The separation of the support ranges by exactly the dimension is what makes the final comparison of supports work. The counted span refers twice to results of other chapters, both carried as navigation stubs.
